title: Silence before false witnesses
source_text: Ὁ μὲν σωτὴρ καὶ κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ψευδομαρτυρούμενος μὲν „ἐσιώπα“ κατηγορούμενος δὲ „οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο“, πειθόμενος πάντα τὸν βίον ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τὰς ἐν Ἰουδαίοις πράξεις κρείττους γεγονέναι φωνῆς ἐλεγχούσης τὴν ψευδομαρτυρίαν καὶ λέξεων ἀπολογουμένων πρὸς τὰς κατηγορίας· σὺ δ᾿, ὦ φιλόθεε Ἀμβρόσιε, οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως πρὸς τὰς Κέλσου κατὰ Χριστιανῶν ἐν συγγράμμασι ψευδομαρτυρίας καὶ τῆς πίστεως τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν ἐν βιβλίῳ κατηγορίας ἐβουλήθης ἡμᾶς ἀπολογήσασθαι. ὡς οὐκ ὄντος ἐναργοῦς ἐλέγχου ἐν τοῖς πράγμασι καὶ πάντων γραμμάτων κρείττονος λόγου, τοῦ τε τὰς ψευδομαρτυρίας ἀφανίζοντος καὶ ταῖς κατηγορίαις μηδὲ πιθανότητα εἰς τὸ δύνασθαί τι αὐτὰς ἐνδιδόντος. περὶ δὲ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὅτι „ἐσιώπα“ ψευδομαρτυρούμενος, ἀρκεῖ ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος τὰ Ματθαίου παραθέσθαι· τὰ γὰρ ἰσοδυναμοῦντα αὐτῷ ὁ Μάρκος ἔγραψεν. ἔχει δ᾿ οὕτως ἡ τοῦ Ματθαίου λέξις· „ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ τὸ συνέδριον ἐζήτουν ψευδομαρτυρίαν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὅπως θανατώσωσιν αὐτὸν, καὶ οὐχ εὗρον πολλῶν προσελθόντων ψευδομαρτύρων. ὕστερον δὲ προσελθόντες δύο εἶπον· οὗτος ἔφη· δύναμαι καταλῦσαι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν οἰκοδομῆσαι. καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ. ὅτι οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐσιώπα.“ ἀλλὰ καὶ ὅτι οὐκ ἀπεκρίνετο κατηγορούμενος, τοιαῦτα γέγραπται· „ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐστάθη ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ἡγεμόνος· καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων· σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔφη αὐτῷ· σὺ λέγεις. καὶ ἐν τῷ κατηγορεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνετο. τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· οὐκ ἀκούεις, πόσα σου καταμαρτυροῦσι; καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ πρὸς οὐδὲν ῥῆμα, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν ἡγεμόνα λίαν.“
pass_a_gloss: The Saviour (σωτήρ) and Lord (κύριος) of us, Jesus Christ, being falsely witnessed against (ψευδομαρτυρέω, pres. pass. ptc.) 'was silent' (σιωπάω, impf.), and being accused (κατηγορέω, pass. ptc.) 'answered nothing' (ἀποκρίνομαι, aor.), being persuaded (πείθομαι) that his whole life (βίος) and his deeds (πρᾶξις) among the Jews had been stronger (κρείττων) than a voice (φωνή) refuting (ἐλέγχω) the false witness (ψευδομαρτυρία) and than words (λέξις) defending (ἀπολογέομαι) against the accusations (κατηγορία). But you, O God-loving (φιλόθεος) Ambrose, I do not know how, wished (βούλομαι) us to make a defence against Celsus's false witnessings against Christians in writings (σύγγραμμα) and his accusation of the faith (πίστις) of the churches (ἐκκλησία) in a book (βιβλίον). As if there were not a clear (ἐναργής) refutation (ἔλεγχος) in the facts/deeds (πράγματα) and a word/reason (λόγος) stronger than all writings (γράμματα), which both makes the false witnesses vanish (ἀφανίζω) and grants (ἐνδίδωμι) to the accusations not even plausibility (πιθανότης) toward being able to do anything. About Jesus, that he 'was silent' when falsely witnessed against, it suffices for the present to set beside (παρατίθημι) the things of Matthew; for Mark wrote things equivalent (ἰσοδυναμέω) to it. The wording (λέξις) of Matthew is thus: [Matt 26:59-63: high priest (ἀρχιερεύς, sing.) and council (συνέδριον) sought false witness against Jesus so as to put him to death (θανατόω), found none though many false witnesses came; later two came and said: this man said, I can destroy (καταλύω) the temple (ναός) of God and through three days build (οἰκοδομέω) it; the high priest stood and said: you answer nothing to what (ὅ τι) these testify against (καταμαρτυρέω) you? But Jesus was silent.] But also that he did not answer (ἀποκρίνομαι, impf.) when accused, such things are written: [Matt 27:11-14: Jesus stood before the governor (ἡγεμών); he questioned (ἐπερωτάω) him: are you the king (βασιλεύς) of the Jews? Jesus said: you say (so). And in being accused by the chief priests and elders (πρεσβύτεροι) he answered nothing. Then Pilate says: do you not hear how many things they testify against you? And he did not answer him to not one word (ῥῆμα), so that the governor marvelled (θαυμάζω) greatly (λίαν).]
pass_b_english: When false witness was borne against our Saviour and Lord Jesus Christ, he “kept silent” (Matthew 26:63); when he was accused, he “answered nothing” (Matthew 27:12). He was convinced that his whole life and his deeds among the Jews were stronger than a voice refuting the false witness, or words of defence against the charges. But you, Ambrose, lover of God, wished, I do not know why, that we should make a defence against Celsus: against the false witness he bore against Christians in his writings, and against the charge he brought in a book against the faith of the churches. It is as if there were no clear refutation in the facts themselves, and no word stronger than all writings, which both makes false witness vanish and does not allow the charges even enough plausibility to have any force.

To show that Jesus “kept silent” when false witness was borne against him, it is enough for the present to quote Matthew, since Mark wrote what amounts to the same (Mark 14:55–61). Matthew’s words run as follows: “The high priest and the council sought false witness against Jesus, so that they might put him to death; and they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. At last two came forward and said, ‘This man said, “I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build it in three days.”’ And the high priest stood up and said to him, ‘Do you answer nothing to what these men testify against you?’ But Jesus kept silent” (Matthew 26:59–63).

And that he did not answer when he was accused is written as follows: “Now Jesus stood before the governor; and he questioned him, saying, ‘Are you the King of the Jews?’ And Jesus said to him, ‘You say so.’ And when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. Then Pilate said to him, ‘Do you not hear how many things they testify against you?’ And he did not answer him a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed” (Matthew 27:11–14).

choices.choice: SOURCE GAP: the staged row (source_pref.json, section 1) is cut off at exactly 1200 characters, ending at 'ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐσιώπα.' and dropping the rest of the chapter. The missing tail was taken from the same Perseus TEI of Koetschau (clients/translations/books/ante-nicene-topics/sources/greek/origen_celsum.xml, Preface ch. 1): 'ἀλλὰ καὶ ὅτι οὐκ ἀπεκρίνετο κατηγορούμενος, τοιαῦτα γέγραπται· „ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐστάθη ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ἡγεμόνος· καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων· σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔφη αὐτῷ· σὺ λέγεις. καὶ ἐν τῷ κατηγορεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνετο. τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· οὐκ ἀκούεις, πόσα σου καταμαρτυροῦσι; καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ πρὸς οὐδὲν ῥῆμα, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν ἡγεμόνα λίαν.“' The third English paragraph translates this tail; the staged row should be re-extracted. Other chapters (2-6) match the TEI in length. Readings: (1) The edition prints 'οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ. ὅτι οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;' I read ὅτι as ὅ τι ('what'), as the clause demands; the Gospel itself has 'οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ; τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;', rendered here as one question. (2) Origen's text of Matt 26:59 has singular 'the high priest' where the Gospel has 'the chief priests'; kept as Origen gives it. (3) In Matt 27:11 Origen's text has 'he questioned him' without naming the governor; kept. (4) 'οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως' is literally 'I do not know how'; rendered 'I do not know why', the English idiom for this mild puzzlement. (5) 'πάντων γραμμάτων κρείττονος λόγου': λόγος may carry a play on the Word; rendered 'word' in lower case to keep both senses without forcing either. No LXX renumbering needed.

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; the English is from the Greek.

changes: Confirmed the staged row is cut at 1200 characters; checked the supplied tail (Matthew 27:11-14) word for word against the Perseus TEI (v.1 p.52) and it matches
'any voice that might refute ... than any words' -> 'a voice refuting ... or words' (φωνῆς ἐλεγχούσης, λέξεων ἀπολογουμένων: no 'any', no 'might')
'leaves the charges not even the plausibility' -> 'does not allow the charges even enough plausibility' (ἐνδιδόντος = grant, allow)
'to show from Matthew' -> 'quote Matthew' (παραθέσθαι = cite); clause order made natural ('To show that Jesus kept silent ...')
'this is what is written' -> 'is written as follows' (τοιαῦτα γέγραπται)
Checked citations: Matthew 26:63 (ἐσιώπα), Matthew 27:12 (οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο), Mark 14:55-61, Matthew 26:59-63, Matthew 27:11-14 all say what is quoted
